Through two games, Sutton has posted only nine targets, catching five for a meager 36 yards. He still has plenty of existing chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo could rekindle it once defenses begin shifting more attention to Waddle, but Sutton figures to be hard-pressed to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2026 for a third straight season. He'll take on a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, though three of them have gone for touchdowns.

name: Jacoby Brissett
outlook: Jacoby Brissett will look to bounce back from a poor performance when Arizona faces the 49ers in Week 3. Brissett recorded just 95 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception Sunday in a loss to Seattle, with that yardage being less than half of his previous low mark across any of his 16 starts for the Cardinals. Still, McBride was able to maintain his rapport with star tight end Trey McBride, as the pair connected for 41 yards and a touchdown through the air. Brissett's path to a rebound isn't an easy one, as San Francisco has given up just 11.8 fantasy points per game to QBs -- the second-fewest in the league -- through two weeks.

name: J.K. Dobbins
outlook: J.K. Dobbins' workload has been limited to begin the season, with just 18 carries for 72 yards through the Broncos' first two games. The veteran back also has yet to see a target, as RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman have been prioritized as pass-catchers. Dobbins picked up a minor hamstring injury in Week 2's win over the Jaguars, but the issue isn't expected to keep him out of the lineup in Week 3. The same can't be said for Harvey, however, who didn't play at all in Week 2 due to his own hamstring strain. Dobbins could split touches with Coleman again in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.

name: Dontayvion Wicks
outlook: Dontayvion Wicks continues to cement himself as the No. 2 wideout in the Eagles offense. Wicks caught five passes for 74 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Wicks was second on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury, and with Dallas Goedert also banged up, Wicks could be one of the chief beneficiaries.

name: Kirk Cousins
outlook: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.

name: Gunnar Helm
outlook: Gunnar Helm is tied for second on the Titans with seven targets through two games, but he has just 41 receiving yards. The 2025 fourth-round pick is locked in as the team's starting TE heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, who just allowed six catches for 54 yards and a TD to Rams TE Terrance Ferguson. Helm is unlikely to match that production considering he has yet to exceed 51 receiving yards in a game while scoring just twice through 18 NFL appearances. Unless second-year Titans QB Cam Ward starts to pick up his passing production, Helm can continue to be ignored in the vast majority of fantasy formats.

name: Michael Penix Jr.
outlook: Michael Penix is slated to make his 2026 debut during the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Atlanta has struggled offensively with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand as the team's quarterbacks over the last two weeks, scoring just 16 total points while Rush and Strand accounted for seven turnovers. However, Penix led the Falcons' offense to 20.6 points per game while throwing for 220.2 yards per game when healthy in 2025, suggesting improvement could be coming. Penix will be in for a tough matchup though, as Green Bay's defense has given up just 19.2 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.

name: Michael Mayer
outlook: Michael Mayer hasn't made much of an impact as the Raiders' top tight end through the first two weeks of the season, catching nine of 11 targets for 55 yards without scoring a touchdown. That role has come while Brock Bowers was recovering from minor knee surgery at the end of training camp, but with Bowers expected to return in Week 3, Mayer will see even his modest volume collapse. If Bowers' 2026 debut does get delayed further, Mayer will still be facing a Saints defense that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end so far.

name: Keenan Allen
outlook: Keenan Allen should get plenty of playing time in Week 3 against the Texans with the Colts' banged-up WR room, but the 34-year-old wideout may not have enough gas in the tank to make much of the opportunity. Allen has exceeded 44 yards just once and failed to score a TD in his last 12 games. Despite that lack of recent production, he's a viable deep-league dart throw, as Indianapolis will be without Alec Pierce (heel) and possibly Ashton Dulin (ankle), leaving Allen as the top option for snaps at WR alongside Josh Downs.

name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
outlook: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.

name: Rome Odunze
outlook: Rome Odunze will look to remain a top look in Chicago's passing offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards against the Vikings in Week 2, and he now sits at a 5-95-0 receiving line across two games. The third-year pass catcher's unimpressive output could continue, given that Tyson Bagent is slotted to start under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Odunze will face a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.

name: Xavier Hutchinson
outlook: Xavier Hutchinson drew nine targets in Nico Collins' (hamstring) absence in Week 2 but turned that into just three catches for 37 yards. Hutchinson figures to maintain a prominent role in Houston's passing game against the league-worst Colts defense in Week 3, especially if Collins remains sidelined. Whether Hutchinson can turn that significant usage into production is another matter, as he has usually failed to capitalize on such opportunities in the past, with only two career regular-season games of 42 or more receiving yards. Hutchinson is in the Week 3 deep-league flex conversation, but his lack of prior production is concerning.

name: Daniel Jones
outlook: Daniel Jones is averaging 188 passing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 3 home game against the Texans. Houston gave up two touchdown passes apiece to star QBs Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, but Jones will be hard-pressed to post his first multi-TD performance of the season considering the Texans boast one of the league's best defenses, having allowed the fewest yards in the NFL last season. The Colts will continue to rely primarily on the legs of star RB Jonathan Taylor, and Indianapolis has an underwhelming group of pass catchers that's expected to be without last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel) for several weeks. Jones has been a non-factor as a rusher since returning from a torn Achilles, with just 14 rushing yards this season. His mediocre passing stats make him an unappealing Week 3 fantasy option, even in multi-QB formats.

name: Tyler Allgeier
outlook: Tyler Allgeier will seek to improve his efficiency on the ground during Arizona's Week 3 visit to San Francisco. Allgeier gained just 10 yards on five carries Sunday in a loss against Seattle, and he's averaging a meager 3.2 YPC through two contests. He paced the Cardinals with 17 carries in the team's season opener, but  Jeremiyah Love jumped ahead with him with nine carries Week 2 and could continue to settle in as the club's clear No. 1 RB moving forward. The 49ers have yielded 4.04 YPC to running backs so far, but that's led to just one rushing TD.

name: Caleb Douglas
outlook: Caleb Douglas' status for the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs is uncertain due to an ankle injury. Douglas played a hefty 85% of the team's offensive snaps before suffering the injury late in Week 2 but recorded just 19 yards after a 94-yard career debut. Should he play, Douglas is a speculative upside play for fantasy teams in need of Week 3 help.

name: Rachaad White
outlook: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.

name: RJ Harvey
outlook: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.

name: Brenton Strange
outlook: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.

name: Jameis Winston
outlook: Jameis Winston will take the reins of the Giants offense in Week 3 versus the Titans. Jaxson Dart suffered a serious knee injury and may not return this year. Winston's performance in relief of Dart last game left much to be desired, as he completed just 11-of-27 passes for 111 yards and an interception. Against Tennessee, at least Winston will have a week to prepare and face a lower-tier defense. The Titans are giving up 233.5 passing yards per game in 2026, which is 20th in the NFL.

name: Chris Godwin Jr.
outlook: Chris Godwin will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Godwin leads Tampa Bay's receiving corps in offensive snaps played (101) and has caught all seven of his targets through two weeks. However, this hasn't translated to much production, as he's accumulated just 86 receiving yards. Expect Godwin to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in a difficult matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 27 receptions to wideouts through two games.

name: Blake Corum
outlook: Blake Corum should continue to be a big part of the Rams' backfield versus the Broncos in Week 3. Against the Giants on Monday Night Football, Corum racked up 79 yards on 12 carries while adding a 13-yard reception. Through two weeks, Corum has 22 carries to Kyren Williams'  23, so the pair appear to be headed for a pretty even workload in 2026. Denver could be vulnerable to both ball carriers, as the Broncos have given up a whopping 5.40 YPC to RBs this season -- third worst in the league.

name: Kalif Raymond
outlook: Kalif Raymond will look to stay involved as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Raymond was a consistent option once again in Week 2 against the Vikings, catching all five of his targets for 40 yards. The veteran wide receiver has now recorded 13 catches for 124 yards on 14 targets through two games. With quarterback Tyson Bagent also slated to get the start under center, Raymond could be a safe target against a middle-of-the-pack Philly defense against WRs (29.4 PPR points per game).

name: Jordan Addison
outlook: Jordan Addison will seek to ramp things up as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Addison bounced back from a zero-catch performance in Week 1 this past Sunday, logging two catches for 21 yards against the Bears. Still, his output is nowhere near sufficient for fantasy owners, especially since he's put up WR2 numbers many times throughout the last three seasons. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers this season, a top-10 mark.

name: Cam Ward
outlook: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.

name: Kenyon Sadiq
outlook: Kenyon Sadiq could be poised for a major breakout for the Jets in Week 3 if Mason Taylor (thumb) is unable to play against the Lions. Sadiq has played just 42% and 38% of the offensive snaps through two games, easing into the rotation after recovering from hernia surgery prior to the year. The Jets' offense isn't prolific, but the matchup with a porous Lions' defense could change that. Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to opposing tight ends in each of the first two weeks and 187 total yards, the second-highest total across the league.

name: Emanuel Wilson
outlook: Emanuel Wilson will look to build upon a big performance when Seattle faces Washington in Week 3. With Jadarian Price suffering a shoulder injury against Arizona on Sunday, Wilson stepped up and led the Seahawks with 21 rushes for 92 yards. Price's injury isn't considered serious, but it's not certain that he'll be able to return to action in Week 3. Whoever leads Seattle's backfield will be looking to score the first rushing touchdown against the Commanders this season.

name: Ryan Flournoy
outlook: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

name: Chig Okonkwo
outlook: Chig Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 for the Commanders. Washington's active tight ends did not fare well, catching a combined two passes for 20 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Okonkwo, even if he is able to suit up.

name: Romeo Doubs
outlook: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.

name: Rashod Bateman
outlook: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 3 matchup against the Cowboys. In the absence of top wideout Zay Flowers (hamstring), Bateman caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's Week 2 loss. He'll likely slide back to a supporting role if Flowers is able to suit up this Sunday. However, if he's unable to do so, Bateman will have the chance to replicate his solid outing versus a Dallas defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) allowed to WRs.

name: Tyjae Spears
outlook: Tyjae Spears is likely to see a handful of touches as usual for the Titans behind Tony Pollard in Week 3, but that projected usage is enough for Spears to earn flex consideration in deeper formats against a Giants defense that has struggled to defend RBs. The Giants just allowed at least 92 scrimmage yards apiece to the Rams' backfield duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, but the Rams boast one of the league's most talented offenses and led the league with 30.5 points per game last season, while the Titans are averaging 15.0 PPG after scoring 16.7 PPG last season. Spears can make big plays happen in space, as he showed in compiling 70 yards on nine touches in last week's loss to the Eagles, though he had just 24 yards on five touches in the season-opening loss to the Jets.

name: Oronde Gadsden
outlook: Oronde Gadsden hasn't logged much volume to begin the season, with just four targets through two games, but he's caught all four for 50 yards and scored his first touchdown of 2026 in the Chargers' loss last week to the Raiders. The second-year tight end's usage could increase significantly in the coming games. Both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar left the Week 2 loss to Las Vegas with injuries that are expected to land them on injured reserve, leaving Gadsden as the only healthy TE on the roster. He doesn't have the blocking skills of his veteran teammates, which could limit how much OC Mike McDaniel is willing to put him on the field, but Gadsden's workload will still increase almost by default unless the team is able to find immediate help from outside the organization. He'll face a Bills defense in Week 3 that ranks in the bottom 10 in catches and receiving yards allowed to tight ends this season.

name: Evan Engram
outlook: Evan Engram had a minimal role in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, catching his only target for 17 yards. The veteran tight end has notched just six targets through two games, and while he did get into the end zone in the season opener, the reduced volume he saw in 2025, his first year in Denver, doesn't look like it will improve in 2026. Engram will take on a Rams defense in Week 3 that's allowed just 64 receiving yards to TEs so far, sixth in the league, and has yet to allow one to score a touchdown.

name: Tre' Harris
outlook: Tre' Harris caught only one pass in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but he made it count, connecting with a scrambling Justin Herbert for a 53-yard gain that set up a third-quarter touchdown. Harris has just a 4-73-0 line on nine targets through two games, but if he continues to show he can gain significant yards after the catch, he could prove to be a good fit for OC Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 2025 second-round pick will face a Bills secondary in Week 3 that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.

name: Wan'Dale Robinson
outlook: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.

name: Malachi Fields
outlook: Malachi Fields finished third in receptions and second in targets for the Giants last game. Despite seeing increased involvement, Fields caught just two passes for just 30 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Fields will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.

name: MarShawn Lloyd
outlook: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more efficient as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Lloyd scored his first career touchdown off a six-yard catch in Week 2, but he also rushed six times for just 20 yards. The inexperienced running back has now averaged just 3.0 YPC off 19 carries this season, which is far from what Green Bay is looking for out of its RB1. Lloyd will also face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a top-10 127 rushing yards to running backs, which could make his job even harder.

name: Greg Dulcich
outlook: Greg Dulcich's opportunities have been limited in Miami's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. Dulcich has four total catches on five targets to open the year, tallying 35 yards. Kansas City has allowed volume to the position through two weeks, surrendering 12 catches and two touchdowns, but just 74 total yards and 4.6 yards per target. Better fantasy options are available.

name: Kendrick Bourne
outlook: Kendrick Bourne appears to have earned a key role in Arizona's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup versus San Francisco. After joining the Cardinals in the offseason, Bourne has recorded 11 targets through two weeks, second-most among Arizona wide receivers. The veteran wideout has logged a 10-86-0 line on those opportunities, as he has established good chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. With that said, Week 3 could be another tough test for Arizona's air game: the 49ers have allowed just a 59.3 percent catch rate to WRs so far, ninth-best in the NFL.

name: Jakobi Meyers
outlook: Jakobi Meyers has been targeted just three times through Jacksonville's first two games. That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.

name: Tommy Tremble
outlook: Tommy Tremble is expected to remain the Panthers' top tight end in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Tremble was overshadowed by Darren Waller in the Week 2 win, as Waller paced Carolina's tight end corps in targets (three), receptions (three), yards (33) and touchdowns (two) Despite this, Tremble played six more Darren Waller (32 to 26), suggesting he's still operating as the Panthers' top TE. Regardless, Tremble could struggle in Week 3 against a Browns defense that's allowed just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position thus far.

name: Kaelon Black
outlook: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.

name: Ted Hurst III
outlook: Ted Hurst is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Despite the return of Jalen McMillan in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, Hurst played a career-high 45 offensive snaps -- 38 more than McMillan. Additionally, Hurst led the team with seven targets, though it led to just two receptions. Regardless, it appears as if Hurst will remain an important piece of the Buccaneers' offense as the season progresses. The rookie wideout will likely struggle but could find success against a Minnesota secondary that's allowed 12.6 yards per completion this season.

name: Kenny Gainwell
outlook: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.

name: Darren Waller
outlook: Darren Waller could remain a valuable part of the Panthers' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Through two games, Waller appears to be the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end, leading the TE room in yards (66), receptions (five) and touchdowns (two). However, having only received five targets through two weeks, Waller is likely a touchdown-or-bust streaming option going forward. He's in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season.

name: AJ Barner
outlook: AJ Barner should again lead Seattle's TE corps in a Week 3 tilt versus Washington. Barner logged a healthy 56 of the Seahawks' 70 offensive snaps Sunday versus the Cardinals, but he finished with just one catch (on one target) for eight yards. Barner did boost his fantasy line considerably with a rushing touchdown, though his three catches for 21 yards through two weeks isn't going to turn many heads. Nonetheless, he could be a sneaky option for Week 3 against a Commanders defense that has already given up four receiving TDs to tight ends, tied for most in the NFL.

name: Brian Robinson Jr.
outlook: Brian Robinson (ankle) will operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Robinson logged 13 touches in Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Panthers, but eight of those came in the fourth quarter -- suggesting he's still firmly the second option at RB. The Alabama product has been efficient, however, averaging 4.1 yards per carry through two weeks. He's also in for a favorable matchup, with the Packers defense allowing 22.9 PPR fantasy per game to RBs this season.

name: Sam Darnold
outlook: Sam Darnold has a chance to return from a glute injury for Seattle's Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. It remains to be seen if the veteran QB will be able to suit up, but he reportedly has been ahead of schedule in his recovery. With Darnold out against Arizona in Week 2, Drew Lock took over and led the Seahawks to a win. Whichever signal-caller starts under center in Week 3 could feast upon a Washington defense that has allowed a 137.0 passer rating this season, the worst mark in the NFL.

name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
outlook: Marvin Harrison will look to bounce back from his Week 2 goose egg when the Cardinals face San Francisco in Week 3. Harrison was targeted by QB Jacoby Brissett just once Sunday in a loss to the Seahawks and finished without a catch. The third-year receiver concerningly has just one catch for 33 yards through two weeks, and perhaps even more distressingly for his fantasy managers, he's drawn only four targets to Michael Wilson's 14 so far. The 49ers rank in the top 10 through two weeks by giving up only 247 receiving yards to wideouts.

name: Braelon Allen
outlook: Braelon Allen's usage remains questionable as the Jets prepare to face the Lions in Week 3. After a run-heavy Week 1 where Allen had 10 attempts, that number was cut in half in Week 2. He has also only seen two targets through two games. Breece Hall remains the workhorse, and the Lions' vulnerability to chunk plays in the passing game could further phase Allen out of meaningful touches, despite Detroit allowing 5.2 yards per carry.

name: DeMario Douglas
outlook: DeMario Douglas' role in New England's struggling passing offense is questionable ahead of a Week 3 game at Jacksonville. In Week 2, Douglas logged just two targets in his first full game without A.J. Brown after a seven-target opener, and he's averaging just 4.8 yards per reception to start the season. Jacksonville is allowing a hefty 10.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but Douglas' inability to stretch the field would require uncharacteristic heavy volume to provide a modest fantasy return.

name: Isaiah Williams
outlook: Isaiah Williams will look to build on an expanding role in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. Elevated to No. 3 on the depth chart with Omar Cooper landing on IR, Williams recorded six targets last week, catching them all for just 34 yards. The Jets' offense is unlikely to score enough to sustain a third viable receiver, but if there were such a matchup, it would be Week 3 against a secondary that's already allowed 437 yards to wideouts through two games.

name: Kayshon Boutte
outlook: Kayshon Boutte had three catches in his second game with the Texans in Week 2 after going without a catch in his team debut. He's probably the best downfield option in the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring), who looks likely to sit out again in Week 3 against the Colts after missing the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati. The Colts have talent in their secondary, led by CB Sauce Gardner, but they are vulnerable to big plays through the air since they often leave their cornerbacks in one-on-one coverage with receivers. Indianapolis has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL this season, so Boutte has starter-level upside in deep leagues for Week 3.

name: Noah Fant
outlook: Noah Fant is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' tight end corps during the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Fant had a surprisingly productive Week 1 outing, catching four of eight targets for 33 yards and a touchdown. However, he didn't see a target in Week 2 while playing on 45 percent of the team's offensive snaps, suggesting he remains firmly behind Juwan Johnson. Additionally, Fant is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Raiders defense that's given up just eight receptions to TEs through two games.

name: Mason Taylor
outlook: Mason Taylor's availability for the Jets' Week 3 matchup with the Lions is uncertain due to a thumb injury that forced him to exit Week 2 early. Taylor didn't record a catch prior to exiting and has only three targets on the season, leaving him with a very questionable role. The matchup could make him a sneaky option if desperate, as Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to the position in each of their first two games.

name: Jalen Nailor
outlook: Jalen Nailor has had a quiet start to his Raiders' tenure, catching four of eight targets for 36 yards through two games without a touchdown. He hasn't been able to get on the same page as quarterback Kirk Cousins, even though the two were together in Minnesota for the first two years of Nailor's career, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Nailor seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.

name: Jahan Dotson
outlook: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as Atlanta's No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has allowed just 8.3 yards per completion this season. Despite Dotson clearly operating as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout this season, he's had little fantasy value, in large part due to the problems at quarterback. With Michal Penix set to return in the Week 3 matchup, Dotson could be more relevant but will likely remain overshadowed by Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson. Dotson could find the end zone, however, as the Packers' defense has already allowed three touchdowns to wideouts in two games, which is tied for the fourth-most in the NFL.

name: Makai Lemon
outlook: Makai Lemon had just one catch in Philadelphia's win over Tennessee. Lemon is battling with Darius Cooper for the No. 3 wideout spot, as Dontayvion Wicks has all but claimed No. 2 for his own. Lemon had just one target last game, while Cooper had three and Wicks managed six. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.

name: Keon Coleman
outlook: Keon Coleman will look to build on a mild breakout when the Bills face the Chargers in Week 3. He hauled in six passes last week, his highest total since Week 1 of 2025, as the Bills lost DJ Moore (shoulder) early in Week 2. The Chargers have been more vulnerable to slot options than bigger outside receivers, and Moore's availability remains in flux. With the Bills offense clicking at all levels, Coleman can still garner enough volume to be a deep-league flex consideration.

name: Jalen McMillan
outlook: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

name: Kaleb Johnson
outlook: Kaleb Johnson could continue to carve out a role as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Johnson saw a huge uptick in usage against the Jets in Week 2, logging eight carries for 32 yards. The second-year ball carrier was the most efficient of Green Bay's RBs, and he could continue to see an early-down role if MarShawn Lloyd remains inefficient. Still, Atlanta has allowed 127 rushing yards to running backs through two weeks, a top-10 mark, which could make Johnson's job tough even if he's the Packers' go-to on the ground.

name: Pat Bryant
outlook: Pat Bryant fell back to earth after a promising season opener, failing to catch his only target in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars. Quarterback Bo Nix made it a priority to get Jaylen Waddle going, and there wasn't much volume available for anyone else. Bryant gained 16 rushing yards on his only carry, but the No. 3 role in the Denver passing game doesn't figure to offer consistent production, and Bryant could face a challenge for the job once Marvin Mims overcomes a foot injury. Bryant will face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of them have gone for touchdowns.

name: Colby Parkinson
outlook: Colby Parkinson has had a quiet start to the season heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. Parkinson logged just one catch Week 1 and followed that with a 2-15-0 receiving line on Monday Night Football. Meanwhile, fellow TE Terrance Ferguson put up a 6-54-1 line, proving that there's room for players at the position to thrive with QB Matthew Stafford -- though who that tight end is could vary on a week-to-week basis. Denver was burned by Travis Kelce for 71 yards in Week 1 but held Jaguars TEs to just 24 receiving yards in Week 2.

name: Justice Hill
outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens travel to face a Cowboys defense in Week 3 that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) allowed to running backs. He tallied two carries for six yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss to the Saints. As long as Derrick Henry, who accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, is healthy, Hill's action will be limited as the No. 2 RB. However, in a contest that is expected to be high-scoring, Hill could contribute as a receiver, but he's still a risky fantasy play outside of deeper leagues.

name: Dyami Brown
outlook: Dyami Brown tied for second on the Commanders last game with six targets. That led to four catches for 21 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Brown and the rest of the Washington offense.

name: Mack Hollins
outlook: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.

name: Emmett Johnson
outlook: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.

name: Calvin Ridley
outlook: Calvin Ridley has drawn just two targets through two games in Tennessee's underwhelming passing game. The Titans don't have a player with more than 80 receiving yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, so Ridley's fantasy value is slim to none as a depth piece behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson. The Giants have struggled to defend WRs, but Ridley is unlikely to get enough passes thrown his way to capitalize on facing the banged-up Giants secondary.

name: Xavier Legette
outlook: Xavier Legette is expected to play a depth role in Carolina's receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Legette had a solid Week 2 performance after putting up a goose egg in Week 1, catching two of four targets for 64 yards. The third-year pro remains firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker in Carolina's receiving corps, as the two have combined for 26 receptions, 380 yards and a touchdown through two weeks. However, Legette could take advantage of a Cleveland secondary that's allowed 10.0 yards per target to opposing WRs heading into Week 3.

name: Josh Oliver
outlook: Josh Oliver will aim to stay involved in Minnesota's passing game against Tampa Bay in Week 3. Oliver stayed active in a low-scoring Week 2 win against the Bears, reeling in his sole target for a 24-yard gain. The supplementary tight end has now amassed three catches for 46 yards off five targets in his first two outings. He'll take on a New York defense that's allowed a third-lowest 6.0 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season.

name: Jauan Jennings
outlook: Jauan Jennings will hopefully return to action as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jennings sat out in Week 2 due to personal reasons, so his practice availability this upcoming week should dictate whether he plays at the Bucs. The former 49ers wideout has yet to record a catch this season, but he played almost 50 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 1. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers so far this season, a top-10 mark.

name: Cooper Kupp
outlook: Cooper Kupp has so far had a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington. Kupp has logged just two receptions in each of the Seahawks' first two games, registering 55 yards across the four total catches. He ranks third on the team with five targets, trailing Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22) and Rashid Sheheed (nine). As those numbers suggest, Smith-Njigba is dominating looks again this season, so Kupp and Shaheed may be left to compete for scraps throughout the campaign. With that said, there may be lots of receptions to go around against the Commanders, who have given up 27 catches to wideouts through two weeks -- tied for third-most in the NFL.

name: Cole Kmet
outlook: Cole Kmet remains a depth option as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Even though Kmet played more offensive snaps in Week 2 (69 percent) than in Week 1 (57 percent), he garnered just one target and was unable to catch it. Still, young tight end Colston Loveland has yet to do much this year, which could keep a veteran presence like Kmet relevant. He'll face a Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).

name: Isaac TeSlaa
outlook: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. TeSlaa recorded his first catches of the season against the Bills in Week 2, reeling in two of five targets for 26 yards. While his final stat line was still modest, the second-year receiver's five targets are promising. With that being said, he still hasn't done enough to be considered more than a depth option, especially against a New York defense that's been tougher on wide receivers so far this year.

name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
outlook: Chris Rodriguez has notched just six rushing attempts in each of his first two games with the Jaguars. He's averaging a paltry 3.0 yards per carry and has yet to earn a target in the passing game, where Rodriguez has been a non-factor his entire NFL career. Bhayshul Tuten has 28 carries this season and is the clear lead back for the Jaguars. Rodriguez isn't an advisable fantasy play in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing a minuscule 8.0 points per game.

name: Jerry Jeudy
outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3, whose defense allowed just 145 yards through the air in Week 2. He failed to corral his lone target during Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2, giving him a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through two games. Meanwhile, rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion combined for 123 yards and one TD while catching 11 of 13 targets, and they look to be the leaders in the WR room. It will be difficult to start any of them until the Browns' offense consistently proves it can sustain any fantasy-relevant players.

name: Samaje Perine
outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with an illness that forced him to miss two days of practice, he was active in Week 2 and recorded two carries for six yards and caught his lone target for 16 yards during Cincinnati's win over the Texans. With backfield mate Chase Brown handling 23 total touches, Perine's limited involvement on offense makes him a solid fantasy insurance policy, but nothing more. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 28th in rushing yards (233) and 29th in receiving yards allowed (97) to RBs.

name: Antonio Williams
outlook: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.

name: Tyquan Thornton
outlook: Tyquan Thornton produced strong numbers in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, hauling in all four of his targets for 86 yards. The fifth-year speedster is at best fifth in the pecking order for looks from Patrick Mahomes, but his role as a deep option gives Thornton some big-play potential in the right matchup, even on limited volume. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.

name: Chris Bell
outlook: Chris Bell will look for a breakout opportunity in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has drawn only three targets through two weeks, resulting in one catch and a declining snap share, playing just 40% of offensive plays last week. A potential absence from Caleb Douglas (ankle) could elevate Bell to a WR2 role in a struggling offense that often throws while playing from behind. Kansas City's pass defense has been stingy, but should Douglas sit, Bell would be an intriguing high-upside option if chasing points in Week 3.

name: Jaylin Noel
outlook: Jaylin Noel could see extra opportunities in Week 3 if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a second consecutive game against the Colts. Noel has just three catches this season, but two of them have exceeded 30 yards. The 2025 third-round pick's big-play ability makes him a viable deep-league option in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two games. Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jared Wayne are the other healthy options in Houston's WR room.

name: Jack Bech
outlook: Jack Bech has been unable to escape a supporting role in the Raiders' offense to begin his second NFL season. Through two games, the 2025 second-round pick has a 5-48-1 line on just six targets, volume that will make it very difficult to make a consistent impact. Bech had to watch journeyman Cody White come off the practice squad and catch two red-zone TDs in a Week 2 win over the Chargers, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Bech seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.

name: Erick All Jr.
outlook: Erick All Jr. and the Bengals travel to face the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After not recording a target in the season opener, All tallied two catches on three targets for five yards in the Week 2 win over Houston. He was on the field for 24 offensive snaps compared to 21 for starter Mike Gesicki, but that trend will have to consistently continue for him to even be considered in fantasy formats. With Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins accounting for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 Week 2 pass attempts, it's going to be hard to trust anyone outside of those two in the passing game, especially against Pittsburgh's second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) to TEs.

name: Keaton Mitchell
outlook: Keaton Mitchell has taken a clear backseat to Omarion Hampton in the Chargers' backfield to begin the season, getting 10 touches to his teammate's 37 through two games. Mitchell has yet to do much to earn a larger role, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, although he does have a 15-yard gain on his only catch. Hampton has lost a fumble in each game so far in 2026, and these ball security issues could open the door for Mitchell to get more involved. If he does see more volume in Week 3, Mitchell could hit paydirt against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.

name: Chris Brooks
outlook: Chris Brooks should continue to stay involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Brooks was a non-factor on the ground against the Jets in Week 2 (four carries for 11 yards), but he did reel in his first catch of the season for 15 yards. The fourth-year running back should remain on the field for passing-situation plays moving forward, especially since he served that role last season even with Josh Jacobs on the field. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's been tough on RBs so far this season, allowing a top-10 16.3 PPR points per game.

name: Andrei Iosivas
outlook: Andrei Iosivas and the Bengals are on the road for a Week 3 meeting versus the Steelers. He caught his only target for seven yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 victory, and it looks like that could be his norm moving forward. Iosivas played 54% of offensive snaps after playing 61% in the season opener. He's clearly behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins in the receiver pecking order and thus should remain on waiver wires in Week 3 against Pittsburgh's second-ranked passing defense.

name: Darnell Mooney
outlook: Darnell Mooney led the Giants in receiving last game.  Unfortunately, Mooney managed just 48 yards on two catches in the 28-6 loss to the Rams. The bigger news is that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Mooney will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.

name: Germie Bernard
outlook: Germie Bernard and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional showdown. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, the rookie stepped into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Bernard caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in the 20-3 loss, seemingly earning the trust of Aaron Rodgers rather quickly. He led the team in yardage, was second in targets, and tied for second in receptions. Bernard faces Cincinnati's 9th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (25.0) to WRs and should be considered a roster stash until we see this type of performance consistently.

name: Tank Bigsby
outlook: Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Bigsby and Will Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.

name: Mike Washington Jr.
outlook: Mike Washington hasn't seen much action to begin his NFL career, getting 10 carries through the Raiders' first two games and turning them into 48 yards. He also failed to bring in his only target. Ashton Jeanty is locked into the top spot in the backfield and has 54 touches, third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker, and unless he gets hurt, Washington's workload figures to be limited. The rookie will look to take advantage of the chances he does get in Week 3 against a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.

name: Kevin Coleman Jr.
outlook: Kevin Coleman remains without a catch through two games as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs. Coleman logged a higher snap share than Chris Bell, and both roles could be elevated if Caleb Douglas (ankle) is unable to play. Miami has completed only 29 passes through two weeks, and the passing game seems unlikely to sustain even a second receiver in a matchup against a Kansas City secondary that's allowing a mere 6.2 yards per target.

name: Sione Vaki
outlook: Sione Vaki should remain Detroit's low-usage RB2 in Week 3 against the Jets. Vaki logged one carry for seven yards and caught one pass for 13 yards against the Bills in Week 2, showcasing that the secondary running back for the Lions is a graveyard role this year. The third-year ball carrier is still on pace to log career-high numbers given his small role so far in his career, but he's nothing more than a depth option with Jahmyr Gibbs healthy.

name: Olamide Zaccheaus
outlook: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving corps during the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Zaccheaus played 29 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is 11 more than he did in Week 1. However, this didn't lead to an increase in production, as he caught just one of three targets for three yards. Zaccheaus could benefit from the return of quarterback Michael Penix in Week 3, but he'll likely have to find the end zone to be fantasy relevant. Additionally, he could struggle against a Packers defense that's given up just 5.4 yards per pass attempt this season, the fifth-best mark in the NFL.

name: Travis Hunter
outlook: Travis Hunter didn't have a target or carry in Week 2 and has played only a handful of snaps on offense for the Jaguars this season. He's off the fantasy radar heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, outside of IDP formats that reward Hunter's contributions as a cornerback. Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers should continue to lead Jacksonville's wide receiver room.

name: Emari Demercado
outlook: Emari Demercado continues to play backup to Javonte Williams following the Malik Davis injury, but Demercado has had a marginal role through the first two games for Dallas. Demercado has five carries for a combined 15 yards behind Williams. Even if he receives a few extra touches, Demercado will have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL.

name: Jonah Coleman
outlook: Jonah Coleman didn't see the ball in his NFL debut during the Broncos' opener, but his role increased in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Coleman ended up getting more touches than J.K. Dobbins, with the 2026 fourth-round pick turning 10 carries into 39 yards and his first career touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 19 yards. It's not clear how much time Harvey might miss, but Coleman's solid showing in his first opportunity could begin the process of turning the backfield into a three-man committee, with the workload dependent on whoever happens to be healthy. Coleman could be a risky play in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.

name: Will Shipley
outlook: Will Shipley managed nine touches for 29 yards in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Shipley and Tank Bigsby would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge, as the latter had 15 touches and a touchdown to outpace Shipley. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears run defense allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.

name: Bryce Lance
outlook: Bryce Lance is expected to remain the Saints' No. 3 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite playing 78 percent of New Orleans' offensive snaps in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Lance drew just one target. He remains far behind Chris Olave and Devaugh Vele in the team's receiving corps, with his role likely diminishing further once Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns from IR. However, Lance, who ran a 4.34 40-yard dash, could find success against a Raiders secondary that's allowed 12.3 yards per completion this season.

name: Kyle Williams
outlook: Kyle Williams hopes for more opportunities in Week 3 as the Patriots face the Jaguars. Rising up the depth chart with A.J. Brown on IR, Williams still only recorded a 21% snap share, registering two targets and a 10-yard catch in Week 2 where New England completed only 14 passes. Williams has big-play potential, but the passing game isn't operating at a high enough level to sustain a No. 4 WR despite facing a defense that's allowing 10.3 yards per target.

name: Joshua Palmer
outlook: Joshua Palmer will look to make another chunk play for the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. Palmer has just two catches on the year, but they've gone for 34- and 43-yard touchdowns. The Chargers are allowing 10.8 yards per target to wideouts, the third highest through two weeks, so while volume isn't likely, Palmer could still contribute.

name: George Holani
outlook: George Holani may be asked to take on a bigger offensive role for Seattle in a Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury late in a Week 2 win against Arizona, and if he isn't able to suit up versus Washington, Holani would figure to see more work, though Emanuel Wilson would presumably take over No. 1 RB duties. As it is, Holani has gotten involved on offense in each of Seattle's contests so far, combining to produce 42 yards on 12 carries and two yards on one reception. The Commanders have been decimated through the air this season, but they haven't surrendered a rushing touchdown so far.

name: Devontez Walker
outlook: Devontez Walker and the Ravens travel to take on the Cowboys in Week 3. The third-year receiver hauled in one of two targets for 47 yards in Baltimore's Week 2 loss, good for third on the team in receiving yards. Rashod Bateman (7-88-1) filled in admirably for Zay Flowers, who sat out with a hamstring injury, but there's a high chance of the latter making his return to the field in Week 3. Walker's fantasy upside remains limited in a run-heavy offense, however, despite a potential shootout in Dallas.

name: Seth McGowan
outlook: Seth McGowan is locked in as the little-used backup to workhorse Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, having beaten out DJ Giddens (knee) for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. McGowan has just two carries and one target through two games. With Taylor healthy for a Week 3 home game against the AFC South rival Texans, McGowan remains a non-factor in fantasy.

name: KaVontae Turpin
outlook: KaVontae Turpin did not even garner a target last game for Dallas. Turpin continues to be utilized largely in the return game. Meanwhile Ryan Flournoy is the clearcut No. 3 wideout behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

name: Ollie Gordon II
outlook: Ollie Gordon's workload could increase if Jaylen Wright misses the Dolphins' Week 3 game against the Chiefs. Despite being No. 3 on the depth chart, Gordon has outsnapped Wright behind Miami's workhorse, De'Von Achane. Kansas City allowed stud Jonathan Taylor to rush for two scores in Week 2 but kept Denver's backs under control in Week 1. Barring an injury to Achane, it's difficult to envision a path to meaningful production for Gordon.

name: Jaylen Wright
outlook: Jaylen Wright's role is limited in the Dolphins' backfield entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. He has logged just seven snaps through two games and is now dealing with a stinger issue that makes him uncertain to play. With no clear immediate path to touches, Wright is an insurance policy in a matchup against a defense allowing 4.0 yards per carry.

name: Zachariah Branch
outlook: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in Atlanta's WR room in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Branch played just 13 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is five less than he logged in Week 1. It appears as if the rookie wideout's primary role is a return man, as he's operated as Atlanta's top punt returner this season. Branch's role could grow as the season progresses, but he's unlikely to find fantasy relevance in Week 3. Additionally, the Packers' defense has given up just 175 passing yards per game this season, making it an unfavorable matchup.

name: Demond Claiborne
outlook: Demond Claiborne is set to be a secondary option at running back once again as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Claiborne did not log a carry as one of Aaron Jones' backups against the Bears in Week 2, but he did reel in his single target for two yards. Still, the rookie running back will remain a depth pick against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.

name: Ray Davis
outlook: Ray Davis has limited involvement in Buffalo's offense entering Week 3 against the Chargers. Through two weeks, Davis has logged one carry and no targets as James Cook's primary backup, making his only contribution on kick returns. Facing a defense that's allowing just 2.98 yards per carry and with no clear path to an uptick in opportunities, Davis is an insurance policy for Cook managers only.

name: Tyler Badie
outlook: Tyler Badie was inactive for the Broncos' opener but worked into the backfield mix during Week 2's win over the Jaguars thanks to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Working as the No. 3 running back behind J.K. Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman, Badie gained just one yard on his only carry but caught two of three targets for 28 yards. Dobbins also picked up a hamstring injury in the win, and while the issue isn't expected to keep him sidelined, the veteran RB's history of injuries makes any appearance on the injury report a cause for some concern. If Badie does see a bigger role in Week 3, he'll be facing a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.

name: Isaiah Bond
outlook: Isaiah Bond and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for a Week 3 tilt. He caught his lone target for 10 yards during Cleveland's shocking victory over Tampa Bay in Week 2. It appears rookie receivers Denzel Boston (5-95-1) and KC Concepcion (6-28-0), along with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. (5-54-0), will be the focal point of the passing game, leaving Bond and Jerry Jeudy as the odd men out. Bond can be left on waiver wires in all formats versus a Panthers defense allowing 30.3 fantasy points (T-15th) to WRs.

name: Odell Beckham Jr.
outlook: Odell Beckham has yet to catch a pass through two games for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Beckham will likely see his stock further take a hit. In Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league, though Beckham looks more like depth than anything else at this point.

name: Tyson Bagent
outlook: Tyson Bagent is set to get the start for Chicago in Week 3 versus the Eagles. With Caleb Williams currently week-to-week with a hamstring injury and doubtful against Philly, Bagent is primed to get his first start since the 2023 season. The D2 product completed five of nine passes for 54 yards in the fourth quarter against the Vikings this past week after filling in for Williams, but he was unable to deliver a win for the Bears in the end. Bagent's most notable stats trail back to 2023, when he completed 94 of 143 passing attempts for 859 yards with three touchdowns and six interceptions across five games while filling in for Justin Fields. He'll face an Eagles offense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.

name: Isiah Pacheco
outlook: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 3 as the Lions take on the Jets. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
